title: OGG1-Binding to Oxidized Guanine Base in Viral DNA Overcomes Epstein–Barr Virus Latency
authors: Wenjing Hao; Xiaoqi Wang; Jiabo Li; Gang Liu; Lang Pan; Xueqing Ba; Istvan Boldogh; Ziyuan Duan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究氧化损伤修复蛋白OGG1与EBV病毒DNA的结合及其对潜伏期再激活的调控，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作体系，但未涉及TF-DNA特异性结合、AI或物理模拟方法，仅提供机制性实验证据，对本课题方法借鉴有限。
abstract: Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) establishes lifelong latency in human cells and can periodically reactivate, contributing to several cancers. However, the molecular mechanisms that disrupt EBV latency, particularly those driven by oxidative stress, require further investigation. In this study, we provide evidence that oxidative DNA damage, particularly the formation of 8-oxoguanine and its repair enzyme OGG1, is involved in EBV reactivation. We demonstrated that OGG1 is recruited to EBV regulatory regions under oxidative stress conditions and is associated with the transcriptional activation of immediate-early and early lytic genes. Further experiments showed that pharmacological inhibition of OGG1 DNA binding significantly suppressed EBV lytic gene expression, supporting a functional role for OGG1 in viral reactivation. Mechanistically, our findings suggest that OGG1 may contribute to EBV lytic activation through a noncanonical mechanism independent of its glycosylase activity. These findings provide insight into how EBV may exploit host oxidative DNA damage responses to facilitate latency disruption and suggest that targeting OGG1 may offer a potential strategy to limit EBV reactivation and EBV-associated diseases. Graphical Abstract The model illustrates how oxidative DNA damage promotes Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) lytic reactivation through host base excision repair machinery Reactive oxygen species (ROS) may induce oxidative modification of guanine to 8-oxoguanine (8-oxoGua) in latent EBV genomes, potentially contributing to OGG1 recruitment to viral regulatory regions. OGG1 binding facilitates the transcriptional activation of immediate-early and early lytic genes, likely through transcription factor recruitment, thereby contributing to the transition from latency to lytic replication. Pharmacological inhibition of OGG1-DNA interaction suppresses this process, highlighting OGG1 as a potential therapeutic target. 8-oxoGua, 7,8-dihydro-8-oxoguanine; OGG1, 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase-1. Significance Statement identifies a potential mechanism by which ROS-induced oxidative DNA base damage and OGG1 recruitment within the EBV genome may contribute to viral reactivation from latency. suggests that oxidative DNA repair intermediates may serve as regulatory platforms for viral gene expression. provides pharmacological evidence supporting OGG1 as a potential therapeutic target for suppressing EBV reactivation.
abstract_zh: EB病毒（Epstein–Barr virus, EBV）在人类细胞中建立终身潜伏期，并可周期性再激活，参与多种癌症的发生。然而，破坏EBV潜伏期的分子机制，尤其是由氧化应激驱动的机制，仍需进一步研究。在本研究中，我们提供证据表明氧化性DNA损伤，特别是8-氧鸟嘌呤的形成及其修复酶OGG1，参与EBV再激活。我们证明，在氧化应激条件下，OGG1被招募至EBV调控区域，并与立即早期和早期裂解基因的转录激活相关。进一步实验显示，药理学抑制OGG1的DNA结合显著抑制EBV裂解基因表达，支持OGG1在病毒再激活中的功能作用。机制上，我们的发现提示OGG1可能通过不依赖其糖基化酶活性的非经典机制促进EBV裂解激活。这些发现揭示了EBV如何利用宿主氧化性DNA损伤反应促进潜伏期破坏，并提示靶向OGG1可能为限制EBV再激活及EBV相关疾病提供潜在策略。图形摘要 该模型展示了氧化性DNA损伤如何通过宿主碱基切除修复机制促进EB病毒（EBV）裂解再激活。活性氧（ROS）可能诱导潜伏EBV基因组中鸟嘌呤氧化修饰为8-氧鸟嘌呤（8-oxoGua），从而可能促进OGG1招募至病毒调控区域。OGG1结合通过转录因子招募促进立即早期和早期裂解基因的转录激活，从而促进从潜伏期向裂解复制的转变。药理学抑制OGG1-DNA相互作用可抑制此过程，凸显OGG1作为潜在治疗靶点。8-oxoGua，7,8-二氢-8-氧鸟嘌呤；OGG1，8-氧鸟嘌呤DNA糖基化酶-1。意义声明 识别了ROS诱导的氧化性DNA碱基损伤及EBV基因组内OGG1招募可能促进病毒从潜伏期再激活的潜在机制。提示氧化性DNA修复中间体可能作为病毒基因表达的调控平台。提供药理学证据支持OGG1作为抑制EBV再激活的潜在治疗靶点。
